Shopping app

A full mobile storefront — browse, search, product detail with variants, cart, checkout and order tracking — designed and built as one continuous flow rather than a set of disconnected screens.

Year
2025
Duration
14 weeks to launch
Our role
Product design, mobile engineering, commerce backend
Platforms
iOS · Android

Context

A retail brand selling through a marketplace wanted its own app, where it owned the customer relationship, the merchandising and the post-purchase experience instead of renting them.

The problem

Mobile storefronts lose buyers between product detail and payment — variant pickers, cart edits and address entry are each a place to drop out.

Variant selection without a dead end

Colour and size live on the product detail screen, not behind a modal. Out-of-stock combinations are visible before they are tapped, so the buyer never selects their way into an error.

A cart people can actually edit

Quantity steppers, per-line removal and a running subtotal with shipping shown before checkout starts — the total never changes shape after the buyer has committed to paying.

Order state after the sale

Processing, shipped and delivered are separate, filterable states in order history, because "where is my order" is the single most common support contact for a new storefront.

How we built it

One flow, designed end to end

Onboarding through order confirmation was designed as a single path before any screen was built, so the checkout was not bolted onto a browse experience late in the project.

Native patterns, shared codebase

React Native with platform-appropriate navigation and a five-tab bar that stays consistent across home, categories, wishlist, cart and profile.

Payment handled by Stripe

Card details never touch the app or our servers. Saved payment methods and addresses are tokenised, which keeps the checkout short on repeat purchases.

Screens

Outcome

One uninterrupted path from browse to confirmed order: inline variant selection, editable cart, saved addresses and payment methods, and an order history the buyer can actually follow.

  • Browse, search, filter, product detail, cart, checkout and order tracking shipped as one release.
  • Checkout reduced to three steps: shipping address, payment method, review and place.
  • Order history with processing, shipped and delivered states, cutting "where is my order" contacts.
